A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same fairness-constrained optimization benchmark. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original ACSIncome optimization and fairness results, including Table 3 and convergence plots. Appendix B reports an additional SSw experiment.

after.justification: Section 4.2 reports original binary- and multi-group experiments. Appendix B additionally reports validation results for extensive hyperparameter comparisons.

M1.justification: The fairness constraint construction is extended from a binary loss difference to each subgroup's deviation from the mean subgroup loss in Equation 4, used in the new multi-group experiment. The optimizer updates, network architecture, and original binary formulation remain unchanged; Algorithms 1–3 match after reference renumbering.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates Oklahoma ACSIncome with race binarized into white/non-white groups. v2 retains this experiment and adds Virginia ACSIncome with five marital-status groups in Section 4.2.2. This substantially broadens the represented population and tests simultaneous fairness requirements beyond the binary-group setting.

E2.justification: The binary experiment retains all six compared methods. The new Virginia experiment introduces SGD with the explicit subgroup-loss deviation penalty in Equation 13, a distinct comparator from the Fairret accuracy regularizer used in the binary experiment.

E3.justification: The Oklahoma split changes from 80/20 train/test to 80/10/10 train/validation/test, with validation-based grid search. Reported settings also change, including SSw objective/constraint steps from 0.5/0.05 to 0.05/0.04 and its tolerance schedule. v2 revises the fairness-gap definitions and introduces the multi-group evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: v1 Appendix B contains one SSw study with equal 0.02 stepsizes. v2 replaces this limited analysis with systematic sensitivity studies across both experiments: SSw stepsize rules, SSL-ALM smoothing and update parameters, Stochastic Ghost parameters, and regularization strengths. Tables 5–12 and Figure 5 provide substantial new evidence.

E5.justification: Main comparisons retain ten runs, table means and standard deviations, and convergence quartiles. v2 omits the previously displayed medians and reports five-run statistics for each tuning configuration, including its averaging procedure. This does not establish an increase in main-experiment repetitions.

E6.justification: The binary results are substantially revised between v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 4; for example, SGD test inaccuracy changes from 0.215 ± 0.002 to 0.209 ± 0.019 under the revised split. v2 also adds multi-group convergence results and extensive validation results. Changed settings and metric definitions prevent interpreting these revisions as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 generalizes the protected-group notation and Equation 4 to multiple groups, introduces aggregate fairness-gap definitions in Table 2, and adds the penalized formulation in Equation 13. These are substantive mathematical extensions, but the convergence-assumption survey and algorithm equations are retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the benchmark, toolbox, algorithm-review, and empirical-comparison contributions, including the same first-benchmark claim. The additional experiments do not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains Fairret's behavior through penalty selection for constraint satisfaction and interprets center-heavy Fairret/SSw predictions as poor objective minimization. It also argues that constrained methods, especially SSL-ALM, show less tuning sensitivity in the multi-group experiment. The general limitations concerning missing guarantees and ethical applicability remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds search grids, selection criteria, 30/60-second tuning budgets, checkpoint intervals, constraint bounds, and the OSQP subproblem solver. A new reproducibility statement describes supplementary code and README instructions; the repository link itself is unchanged. Some selected settings conflict with the main text, limiting reproducibility despite the substantial additional documentation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cooper, described as the closest toolbox, and Ramirez et al.'s constraints-versus-penalties position paper. Dwork et al.'s Fairness through Awareness reference is removed alongside the Table 1 labeling revision. The broader literature review and positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The five-section main narrative and much of the prose are retained. v2 makes localized rewrites, separates binary and multi-group experiments, moves detailed binary fairness discussion to Appendix A and pseudocode to Appendix C, and adds a reproducibility section.

P2.justification: v2 merges the separate binary train/test convergence figures into overlaid plots, reorders method columns, adds a multi-group convergence figure, and relocates/redraws prediction distributions and radar plots. The radar plots gain a difference-in-accuracy axis. A fairness-definition table and eight tuning tables accompany substantial typography and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens v1's limited evaluation through validation-based tuning, multi-group coverage, and extensive sensitivity evidence. However, new reporting conflicts affect central conclusions: Virginia SSL-ALM uses tau = 0.01 in Section 4.2.2 but tau = 0.05 in Appendix B.2.2, while Table 4 reports worse test sufficiency for ALM than SGD despite the discussion claiming improvement. These reproducibility and interpretation problems make the net quality direction uncertain.
